subject: BUG-264 CRITICAL: syncProgress mints XP from unverified caller input - no rules change can fix it
description:
PROVEN IN PRODUCTION by Mallory 2026-09-06, AFTER both BUG-262 and BUG-263 were live. Those two closed the Firestore-rules-governed direct-write channel and did so cleanly (all forgeries now 403, incl. nested fieldPaths and documents:commit fieldTransform variants). They could not have closed this: syncProgress is a firebase-admin CALLABLE and bypasses firestore.rules BY CONSTRUCTION. Neither commit touched functions/index.js. REPRODUCTION, no Firestore write involved at all: fresh anonymous account with ZERO real gates (verified against the users/{uid}/gates ledger, size 0) -> syncProgress({achievements:['gate_1'..'gate_8']}) -> HTTP 200, xp=4000, level=9, achievements persisted verbatim. deriveXP's gatePattern (functions/index.js:1422-1428) awards 500 XP per matching string with ZERO cross-check against users/{uid}/gates, the ledger completeGate and validateGateAnswer actually write. Same for content: syncProgress({modulesCompleted:['shield-totally-fabricated-never-existed-9999','forge-fake-lab-id-8888'], quizzes:{'never-taken-exam-7777':{score:100}}}) -> HTTP 200, xp=800, level=4, both fabricated ids persisted. sanitizeStringArray/_isValidModuleId check SHAPE ({house}-{key} against a known-house list), never EXISTENCE; sanitizeQuizzes checks the score is 0-100, never that the quiz is real or was ever graded. THE GUARANTEE BROKEN: a student can mint arbitrary XP, level and completion claims through the platform's one intentionally-trusted server endpoint. XP gates skill-tree unlocks and feeds an instructor-facing Completion Evidence export, so this is a forgeable competence claim, which is the never-client-grade rule under another name. NOT SWEPT: labsCompleted and streak via the same callable route (code inspection says they share the missing validation; no standalone reproduction was run). DETECTION, read-only across all 3858 production users docs: (A) streak > days since createdAt -- impossible for an honest client, 3 accounts; (B) achievements claiming gate_N/dark_arts_gateN cross-checked against the real users/{uid}/gates ledger -- 17 accounts claim gates, ALL 17 have at least one unbacked claim, several backed:0 against 5-10 claims. Floor of 20/3858 = 0.5%. IT IS A FLOOR NOT A CEILING: neither signature catches forged modulesCompleted/labsCompleted/quizzes, which need a cross-reference against the canonical content catalog -- that check does NOT exist yet and is the known detection gap. Existing functions/audit-all-xp.js does NOT catch this class: it compares stored xp to deriveXP(stored arrays), and a laundered doc is self-consistent because its xp genuinely equals deriveXP of its forged arrays. FIX MUST BE SERVER-SIDE VALIDATION IN syncProgress, and it is NOT a quick edit: over-strict validation would DELETE legitimate progress for real students, especially legacy accounts whose ledgers may be incomplete. Design before building; the four-way vote applies.
[2026-09-07 00:27] SECOND CALLABLE, WORSE THAN THE FIRST. Mallory proved live 2026-09-06 that recordProgress (functions/index.js:1225) validates NOTHING beyond auth != null and itemId being a non-empty string -- not existence, not format, not source. Reproductions, no Firestore write and no outbox involved: recordProgress({type:'achievement',itemId:'gate_1'}) -> HTTP 200, achievements=['gate_1'], real gates ledger still size 0. recordProgress({type:'module',itemId:'anything-i-want-not-even-house-shaped'}) -> HTTP 200, persisted -- this is WORSE than syncProgress, which at least applies _isValidModuleId's shape check; recordProgress applies nothing. recordProgress({type:'quiz',itemId:'never-graded-by-server-exam',score:100}) -> HTTP 200, quizzes.{id}={score:100} while quiz_attempts is size 0: a THIRD parallel path to a fabricated passing grade that never touches gradeQuiz and never consults quiz_keys or quiz_attempts. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX PLAN: my proposed Stage 1 (have recordProgress ALSO write an append-only users/{uid}/completions witness) would have built A SECOND FORGEABLE LEDGER, not a trustworthy one -- same function, same absent validation, new location. The CTF precedent is trustworthy because validateFlag verifies a submission against a server-held secret BEFORE writing the capture doc; copying flag_captures' shape without copying that verification is copying the part that does not matter. That is form-not-function, and it is exactly what the Chris gate exists to catch. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE INTERIM MITIGATION: my proposal to have syncProgress refuse gate_N achievement strings was UNDERSCOPED and trivially bypassed by calling recordProgress with the same payload. Any interim mitigation must patch BOTH callables in the SAME change. Confirmed safe to do: no legitimate caller anywhere in _app sends type:'achievement' to either callable -- FirestoreManager's three real callers are module, lab and quiz only. ALSO: recordProgress has NO rate limit, unlike validateGateAnswer's explicit 5/60s, so its subcollection can be flooded with attacker-named docs. Cheap separate hardening item.
[2026-09-07 00:29] FOURTH HOLE CONFIRMED, predicted by Nancy from code reading and verified: recordProgress does NOT clamp quiz score. functions/index.js:1283 is 'quizScore = parseInt(score) || 0;' -- client-supplied, no upper bound, no 0-100 clamp -- and functions/quiz-score-policy.js:86 buildQuizUpdate writes newScore straight through into quizzes.{itemId}={score,passedAt}. syncProgress's sanitizeQuizzes DOES clamp 0-100; recordProgress does not, so it is worse again. And because shouldReplaceStoredScore treats a higher score as better, a forged 999999 OVERWRITES a real earned score rather than being ignored. VOTE OUTCOME 2026-09-06: 4-0 AMEND (Nancy, Mallory, Chris, primary). The plan's capstone claim was FALSE: 'Stage 4 closes BUG-264' merely relocates the front door from syncProgress to recordProgress, because recordProgress validates NOTHING beyond auth and a non-empty string itemId. All three reviewers found this independently. THE BEST INTERIM FIX WAS ALREADY IN THE CODEBASE AND I WALKED PAST IT: completeGate (index.js:214-274) already writes users/{uid}/gates/gate{N} with verified/source provenance and an HMAC proof chain for gates 1-5, and deriveXP (index.js:1421-1428) IGNORES it, grepping the client-mergeable achievements array for gate_\d+ strings instead. Pointing that one line at the existing subcollection closes the proven exploit today at zero schema cost, matching a shipped precedent -- a correct derivation rather than my proposed 'block gate_N strings' stopgap. DO NOT FLIP IT BLIND: Mallory measured 17 accounts holding gate_N in achievements with NO matching gates/gateN doc, so switching the source without reconciling them first would zero real earned XP for all 17 -- precisely the BUG-265 harm the whole capture-first redirect exists to prevent. OTHER AMENDMENTS ACCEPTED: (1) Stage 2's metric as designed measures nothing -- if the witness is written inside recordProgress in the same call as the array write, witness-count equals array-length BY CONSTRUCTION; it measures one function's internal consistency, not client-to-server capture loss, so it needs an upstream comparison (outbox depth, beacon, reconciliation sample). (2) 'Stage 1 is additive' was asserted, not verified: making itemId a doc-ID segment introduces failures that do not exist while it only lands in arrayUnion -- a '/' parses as a path separator, IDs over 1500 bytes and IDs matching ^__.*__$ are rejected, so a malformed itemId that used to land harmlessly can now throw and abort a callable that previously succeeded. (3) Subcollection shape may be wrong for COST: flag_captures fires on rare box solves, completions fire constantly on the hottest write path in the platform; a witness FIELD on the existing user-doc write costs zero extra documents versus a per-completion doc across 3858 users forever. (4) recordProgress has no rate limit, unlike validateGateAnswer's 5/60s.
[2026-09-07 01:05] RECONCILIATION RUN 2026-09-06, READ-ONLY, and it OVERTURNS the panel's recommended interim fix. Tool: functions/audit-gate-achievement-backing.js (@catalog TOOL, no write verbs, prints shape only, never a uid). RESULTS across 3870 production users: 17 accounts claim at least one gate achievement -- 4 fully backed by the ledger, 1 partially, 12 with ZERO backing. 102 unbacked claims in total, worth 51000 XP at 500 each. Of the 13 accounts holding unbacked claims: 9 LEGACY (created before the ledger existed on 2026-02-20, commit a17a4afbe) and 4 SUSPECT (created after, so history does not explain the gap); 0 had an unparseable createdAt. THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE PLAN: there are only EIGHTEEN gate docs in the ENTIRE platform, and every single one carries exactly {completed, completedAt, gateNumber} -- NO verified field, NO source field. completeGate (index.js:214-274) writes 'verified: !clientAttested' and 'source: client-attested|server', so NOT ONE of the 18 existing docs was written by the current code path; they all come from an older writer. CONSEQUENCE: repointing deriveXP's gate term at users/{uid}/gates -- which Nancy and Chris both proposed as the best interim fix, and which I agreed with -- WOULD BE DESTRUCTIVE TODAY. The ledger is not merely missing 17 accounts' entries; it is almost entirely unpopulated (18 docs against 102 claims) and what exists carries no provenance to distinguish server-validated from client-attested. Flipping the source would zero roughly 51000 XP, most of it from the 9 legacy accounts that earned it before the ledger existed. Nancy's 'do not flip this blind' condition was correct and the magnitude is worse than anyone estimated. REVISED ORDER: the gates ledger is itself subject to BUG-265 -- it needs capture before it can be an authority. Populate/backfill it (and establish why completeGate's writes are absent from all 18 docs -- is completeGate even reachable from the live gate UI?) BEFORE any deriveXP repoint. Until then the achievements array, forgeable as it is, is the only record of gate completion that actually exists.
[2026-09-07 12:55] WHY BUG-264'S CORE IS NOT A PATCH: THERE IS NO CANONICAL REGISTRY OF VALID COMPLETION IDS. Measured 2026-09-07 against the production snapshot (7528 real completion ids, 3874 users) before attempting existence validation. Deriving a canonical set from content gives at best 55.1% coverage -- 3383 real completions across 415 distinct ids would be REJECTED, including cloud-openstack-neutron (32 students), forge-raid-config (30), web-network-essentials (30). Shipping existence validation on that basis would destroy far more student work than the forgery it prevents. That is the third time tonight that verifying a change against real data stopped one that would have deleted real progress. WHY COVERAGE IS SO POOR: completion ids are DATA-DRIVEN, not literals. _app/path-view.html:437 pushes straight to progress.completedModules with a moduleId derived from URL params and LearningPaths lookups, bypassing ModuleProgress.complete entirely -- so grepping call sites finds almost nothing (0.7% on its own). The id universe is spread across LearningPaths.PATHS (634 declared ids), 271 box trackerKeys, literal ModuleProgress.complete pairs, and pages that construct ids at runtime. No single source of truth exists. THE VIABLE PATH, and it has precedent in this repo: build the registry the way the Hex OS app manifest is built. _tools/hexos/gen-app-manifest.js generates a manifest from sources and deploy.sh gate 3.8 runs it with --check so a stale manifest BLOCKS the deploy. Do the same for completion ids: (1) a generator that unions every declared source PLUS the 572 distinct ids real students already hold, which covers 100% of existing real work by construction; (2) exclude the single known-garbage id forge-forge-core2-virtualization-lab explicitly, documented, rather than blessing it silently; (3) wire the generator into the deploy gate with --check so shipping new content without regenerating the registry fails the build -- otherwise tomorrow's new module is rejected for every student who completes it, which is the same data-loss failure in a new coat; (4) ONLY THEN add existence validation to recordProgress and syncProgress, verified against a fresh snapshot showing 0 real ids rejected. Steps 1-3 are the actual work. Step 4 is three lines.
[2026-09-07 14:25] ENFORCEMENT SHIPPED, BROKE PRODUCTION, AND WAS REVERTED WITHIN THE HOUR 2026-09-07. Read this before re-enabling anything. WHAT BROKE: the registry generator scans for ModuleProgress.complete('house','key') with LITERAL strings. At least 74 shipping pages -- the entire AI-102 certification series, AI Agents, AI Automation, AI Cortex -- call it as ModuleProgress.complete(HOUSE_ID, MODULE_ID) with VARIABLES, which the regex structurally cannot see. Those ids are absent from the registry, from LearningPaths, and from the legacy floor. Reproduced live by the exploit auditor with the exact call a real page makes: recordProgress -> HTTP 400 'Unknown module id.', syncProgress -> HTTP 200 but SILENTLY dropped, syncClassProgress -> HTTP 400. A student finishing AI-102 got no XP, no cross-device sync, and no gradebook entry, with the sync failure invisible. REVERTED to report-only (_ENFORCE_COMPLETION_REGISTRY = false); every unknown id now logs with its value. Verified after revert: all three calls return 200 and the ids land, the four already-working surfaces still record, and the log line fires with the exact id in all three functions. MY ERROR, AND IT IS THE ONE TO REMEMBER: I verified the registry against ids students ALREADY HOLD and reported 100% coverage on every surface. That is 100% of a SNAPSHOT -- a record of the past. It says nothing about content whose ids the generator cannot parse, and new or low-uptake content is precisely what a snapshot under-represents. COVERAGE OF EXISTING DATA IS NOT COVERAGE OF EXISTING CONTENT. The check I should have run first is the one the auditor ran after: grep every ModuleProgress.complete call site for the variable pattern and resolve it. WHAT RE-ENABLING REQUIRES, in order: (1) extend gen-completion-registry.js to statically resolve variable-based call sites -- the auditor resolved 74 of 124 files, 50 remain and need per-file reading; (2) harvest the report-only production logs, which now name every missing id from real traffic rather than from a guess; (3) re-verify that zero legitimate ids are missing, using CONTENT as the denominator and not the snapshot; (4) only then flip _ENFORCE_COMPLETION_REGISTRY to true. THREE SEPARATE GAPS STILL OPEN, all proven, none fixed: syncProgress's localQuizzes has NO registry filter at all (fabricated quiz ids were never guarded by this work, and my brief to the auditor wrongly claimed they were); submitEDTLab writes edt_submissions/{labId}_{uid} BEFORE the registry check, so a rejected forgery still leaves an orphaned doc in an instructor's grading queue; and quiz score forgery is untouched -- a never-earned 100 on a REAL quiz id still overwrites a genuine 72 because shouldReplaceStoredScore is higher-wins.
[2026-09-07 15:56] QUIZ SCORE FORGERY CANNOT BE FIXED THE OBVIOUS WAY -- MEASURED 2026-09-07 BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING. The proposed fix was to ignore the caller's score and read the student's best score from users/{uid}/quiz_attempts, which gradeQuiz writes server-side. Measured against production first: of 1530 stored quiz scores across 99 users, only 395 (25.8%) have a matching quiz_attempts document. Sourcing from the ledger would DESTROY 1135 real grades across 237 distinct quizzes -- eth-w1-quiz for 22 students, core2-ch19-index for 20, openstack-intro-quiz for 18. Only 70 of the 99 users with quiz scores have ANY attempt doc at all. So quiz_attempts is NOT an authority; it is a sparse sample, for the same reason BUG-265 exists -- grading happens but the evidence is not reliably recorded. THAT IS THE REAL BLOCKER, and it is upstream: gradeQuiz must reliably write quiz_attempts BEFORE any consumer can derive from it. Same shape as the completion-registry problem: the ledger cannot become the source of truth until it captures. WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND UNFIXED: a client can claim any score in [0,100] on a REAL quiz id, and because shouldReplaceStoredScore is higher-wins, a fabricated 100 OVERWRITES a genuinely earned 72. Proven live twice. A NARROWER FIX WORTH CONSIDERING LATER, not built tonight: refuse only the OVERWRITE case when the new score has no backing attempt -- that protects grades already earned without rejecting a first-time claim, and needs no ledger completeness. It does not stop initial forgery, only the destruction of real evidence, which is arguably the worse half. Do not build it without first measuring how many legitimate score INCREASES lack a backing attempt, or it will freeze real students at their first score.
